source.title: Dissociating communicative success from representational alignment in common ground formation
source.authors: Taiki Yamamoto; Junya Morita; Ryuichiro Higashinaka; Yugo Takeuchi

record.tranche_reason: The study reports that referential success can improve while its operational measure of representational alignment declines, and that this result varies with the similarity measure.
record.gate_note: The study measures feature-space similarity between sender- and receiver-generated images in a repeated tangram task. It does not test convergence across model scale, independently trained model families, or vision-language models on paired images and captions. Cited findings from other work and the ViT's ImageNet Sketch accuracy are not recorded as results here.
record.test_reason: The study's 'representational alignment' is the cosine similarity between images generated by a sender and a receiver agent in a tangram reference game. It is a communication-alignment construct between interacting pipelines built from the same pretrained modules. It is not alignment between the internal representations of independently trained models, across scale, across seeds, across modalities on paired data, or of shared features. No version names this behaviour, so the study tests none of them and does not cite the original sources. The metric robustness checks (CLIP, Euclidean, silhouette) concern this proxy, not measured cross-model convergence, so they do not bear on V6. The lack of improvement in alignment over trials does not bear on V7.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors also conclude that perceptual-module learning tends to preserve representational alignment. They attribute the dissociation to discriminative learning reusing a dominant expression across rotations, and they stress that their measure is only a proxy.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses a staged tangram communication model and measures cosine similarity between generated images, rather than testing the scale-based model-representation convergence methods in the cited original sources.
record.method_sensitivity: The representational-alignment outcome differs between learned feature-space measures and silhouette-based shape measures. The learning target and presence of discriminative learning also affect symbolic and representational alignment differently.

fits_no_version.finding: With language-module learning plus discriminative learning, referent-identification accuracy rises from 0.338 to 0.945. Over the same trials, similarity between sender- and receiver-generated images falls from 0.370 to 0.260. The perceptual-learning conditions relatively preserve image similarity, and no condition clearly improves it.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In iterated reference games between generative agents, communicative success can rise while similarity between the agents' generated representations declines.

fits_no_version.finding: The decline in image similarity is reproduced with CLIP and with Euclidean distances and with SDXL as the image generator, while silhouette shape metrics stay stable.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The communication–representation dissociation shows up in learned feature spaces, not in low-level shape similarity.

record.problems: Representational alignment is an indirect proxy based on generated-image similarity, not a direct measure of shared understanding. The study uses a fixed-role, single-turn referential task with sender-side updates only. The main text provides no numerical results for most condition trajectories or alternative-metric analyses, and the authors note that results may depend on the selected component models.
record.rows_left_out: No additional relevant results left out. Cited results from prior work and lexical-structure metrics were not included because they do not measure the listed representation-alignment versions.

untested.parts: All: no models of different scale, architecture or data are compared.
All: no vision–language alignment on paired image–caption data as models improve.
All: no comparison of seeds or initializations at the level of features.
All: no mapping, stitching or relative representations between models.
All: no universal features or circuits.
All: the metric comparisons apply to a generated-image similarity proxy, not to cross-model representational convergence.
All: no measure of the degree of cross-model convergence or of its causes.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's 'tests/T5' classification rests on the shared phrase 'representational alignment'. The construct here is inter-agent communicative alignment, not convergence of representations across models. The reader's V6 and V7 labels are removed.

versions.untested_parts: Model scale, capability, and convergence across independently trained models with different architectures, objectives, or data.
Alignment between vision and language models on paired images and captions as the models improve.
Convergence across random initializations of the same architecture and shared features or subspaces.
Mapping representations between models, stitching, relative representations, or alignment without paired data.
Recurrence of interpretable features or circuits across models.
The study varies feature-space metrics but does not test neighbour-count settings or out-of-distribution inputs.
The study does not establish whether shared training data or objectives cause alignment, nor does it test alignment across model scale. Its agents interact and learn in a fixed-role task.

rows.subject: Staged sender–receiver tangram model
rows.stage_stated: Sender-side learning across 10 trials; 20 independent runs
rows.operation_detail: Update the sender's language module and apply discriminative learning; measure representational alignment across trials.
rows.measure: Representational alignment: cosine similarity between sender- and receiver-generated image features from a fixed evaluation ViT
rows.uncertainty: t(19) = −9.82, p < .001, dz = −2.20; Figure 2 shows 95% confidence intervals across runs
rows.note: The feature-space similarity declines even as symbolic alignment improves in this condition.
rows.check: Measures similarity between sender- and receiver-generated images in a communication game. That is not cross-model representational convergence, so V7 does not apply. The value and baseline (0.370 to 0.260) are correct.
